title: SCS Major Intro Mini
description: A short first-year course (a half-semester "mini") that introduces one of the majors in a school of computer science, such as computational biology, human-computer interaction, or robotics. It gives an overview of the field and its typical problems.

title: Humanities and Arts Elective
description: A course chosen from the humanities, social sciences, or fine arts, such as history, philosophy, economics, languages, or music. Together these courses give breadth outside science and engineering.
notes: CMU: 63 units in all, per the SCS General Education Requirements.

title: Science/Engineering Course
description: A course from a college of science or engineering, such as physics, chemistry, biology, or an engineering discipline, chosen to give a computer scientist exposure to another technical domain.

title: Minor Requirement / Free Elective
description: A course toward a required minor (outside computer science) or concentration (within it), or any other course the student chooses.
notes: CMU: the degree requires a minor or an SCS concentration.

title: CS Domains Elective
description: An upper-level computer science course in an area not covered by the program's other required categories, such as computer graphics, computer security, software engineering, or computational biology.
notes: CMU: one course from a list of eight.

title: Probability Course
description: A course in probability for computer scientists or mathematicians: random variables, distributions, expectation, conditional probability, and limit theorems, often with applications to computing.
notes: CMU: one of several probability courses.

title: CS Logic/Languages Elective
description: An upper-level course on rigorous reasoning about programs and systems, such as programming language foundations, logic, program verification, or program analysis.
notes: CMU: one course from a list of eight.

title: Technical Communications Course
description: A course in professional and technical communication: writing for technical and general audiences, presentations, and team communication, sometimes centered on computing research or ethics.

title: CS Software Systems Elective
description: An upper-level, project-heavy systems course, such as operating systems, compilers, distributed systems, networking, parallel programming, or database systems.
notes: CMU: one course from a list of six (min. 12 units).

title: CS Artificial Intelligence Elective
description: An upper-level course in artificial intelligence, such as machine learning, natural language processing, deep learning, computer vision, or robotics.
notes: CMU: one course from a list of nine.

title: SCS Elective
description: An upper-level elective chosen from the courses of any department in the school of computer science.
notes: CMU: two courses, 200 level or above, at least 9 units each.
